source: Kaggle notebook outputs, 2026-11-16. Only values observed in that output are filled in; null means not yet recorded.

gpu.experiment_policy: Use exactly one GPU for every run: set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 before any CUDA library loads, and record it.

packages.torch: 2.14.0 (the vllm install replaced the 2.11.0+cu130 that was preinstalled)
packages.vllm: 0.34.0 from Step 7 on (Steps 2, 5 and 6 ran on 0.33.0)

engine.name: vLLM
engine.status: smoke test passed on the T4 in fp16 (one GPU, pinned revision)
engine.attention_backend: TRITON_ATTN (vLLM chose it out of TRITON_ATTN and FLEX_ATTENTION; FlashInfer top-p/top-k sampling is unavailable on compute capability 7.5, so vLLM falls back)
engine.benchmark_launch_flags_verified: vllm serve accepted --revision, --tokenizer-revision, --dtype float16, --max-model-len, --gpu-memory-utilization, --no-enable-prefix-caching, --enforce-eager (echoed in the server log non-default args, 2026-11-16)

smoke_test_vllm.note: Smoke test, not a benchmark. One untimed request.

engine_reported.source: vLLM startup log lines (engine-reported, measured by the engine)

log_notes: Many warnings 'Attempted to load weight ... bfloat16 into parameter ... float16' appear at load. They are the expected bf16-to-fp16 conversion of a bf16 checkpoint, not errors.
The attention backend (TRITON_ATTN) was read from the Step 5 server log.

step5_first_run.result: 2 requests ok (1 warmup, 1 measured); measured record usable_for_analysis=true, prompt_tokens 1024 matched the workload manifest, 128 output tokens, finish_reason length
step5_first_run.single_measurement_note: n=1. Not a finding. TTFT 0.398 s, e2e 4.621 s, decode 30.1 tok/s for one request.
step5_first_run.server_settings: max_model_len 1216 (auto: 1024 + 128 + 64), gpu_memory_utilization 0.85, enforce_eager true, prefix caching off
step5_first_run.estimator_cross_check_2: 333,904 tokens x 28,672 bytes = 8.9163 GiB vs engine-reported 8.92 GiB
step5_first_run.pool_size_note: The cache pool was 8.92 GiB here versus 8.68 GiB in the max_model_len 4096 smoke test, because vLLM's startup profiling measured a different peak activation (0.23 vs 0.48 GiB). Cache capacity therefore depends on the max_model_len the server is launched with.

estimator_cross_check.reading: The analytical estimate reproduces the engine-reported cache capacity to within rounding for this configuration. This is one data point and supports H4; it does not prove it generally.

step6_validation_run.purpose: Validate the GPU, engine /metrics, and CPU samplers on real hardware. Not a baseline.
step6_validation_run.launch_flag_confirmed: --generation-config vllm was accepted (non-default args in server.log show generation_config 'vllm') and the 'overridden by the model's generation_config.json' warning is gone.
step6_validation_run.gpu_sampler: NVML, 113 samples at a 0.25 s interval (max gap 0.2515 s), 0 read errors

device_memory.note: Device memory is nearly flat and retained between requests. It does not track KV-cache occupancy (31.5 MiB to 115.5 MiB of cache in use vs a roughly 9 GiB pool).

step6_validation_run.engine_cache_usage_check: usage = ceil((prompt + output - 1) / 16) / (total_blocks - 1) reproduced all four measured requests to six digits (inferred: 16-token blocks, one reserved block, last token not cached)

observed_not_conclusions.first_request_cold_start: the 37-token warmup took 2.83 s to its first token while the engine showed 0 running requests and the GPU was about idle; consistent with a one-off CPU-side first-use cost, cause not determined
observed_not_conclusions.prefill: TTFT 0.30-0.38 s at 1024 tokens vs 3.07-3.13 s at 4096 tokens (about 3000 vs 1320 prompt tokens/s); consistent with TTFT growing faster than input length (H1), to be tested with more trials and levels
observed_not_conclusions.decode: about 32 tok/s at both lengths with the GPU about 49-61% busy in eager mode, which suggests decode is not GPU-bound; to be tested by an eager vs CUDA-graph comparison
observed_not_conclusions.ram_view: /proc/meminfo showed 27.4 GiB available (31.3 GiB total) while vLLM's startup log said 3.85 GiB available RAM

step7_pilot.purpose: Pilot for Step 7: 1K/4K/8K input, 2 prompts per level, 3 trials (n = 6 per level), enforce_eager OFF, max_model_len 32768, 128 output tokens forced, per-level warmup, rotated level order. Not a baseline.
step7_pilot.ENGINE_PIN_DECISION: RESOLVED 2026-11-17: the study is pinned to vLLM 0.34.0 from Step 7 on (configs/requirements.lock.txt, regenerated from the pilot session pip freeze; full freeze in configs/kaggle_pip_freeze_2026-11-17.txt; the freeze was taken in the session after the pilot and showed no install was needed, so it is taken to be the pilot stack). Steps 2, 5, 6 data stay labelled 0.33.0. Guard: python -m benchmarks.envcheck, and run manifests store package_versions and lock_mismatches.
step7_pilot.ENGINE_VERSION_DRIFT: How it happened: the server log reports vLLM 0.34.0 although this file pins 0.33.0. The Kaggle session was reset, the unpinned pip install vllm took the newest release, and torch/transformers versions for this run were not recorded. Fixed in code (the manifest now records installed versions); the pin must be decided and the lock regenerated from a printed pip freeze.
step7_pilot.vllm_0_34_changes_seen: extensible KV cache (pool sized after warmup and graph capture; 'Extended KV cache to 4832 blocks'), 64-token blocks (309,248 tokens / 4832 blocks); Step 5/6 runs on 0.33.0 had 16-token blocks by the usage formula
step7_pilot.eager_on_run: Run 20261117T040952Z-6f8b82fb (pinned stack, raw files committed). An earlier eager-on run, 20261117T032011Z-6f8b82fb, exists only as a pasted summary and is not data here.
step7_pilot.repeat_run: Eager-off repeated as 20261117T041433Z-acb4745b with the same config hash; per-level medians agree with the first run within 1 percent (largest difference 0.87 percent, decode at 8K). Cannot say whether the session or the physical GPU was the same.
step7_pilot.cross_mode_outputs: 8 of 10 prompts are bit-identical across eager-on, eager-off and the repeat. Both 8K prompts differ between eager and graphs only in the last few characters (about token 125 of 128); graphs-vs-graphs and eager-vs-eager are exact.
step7_pilot.kv_pool: final pool 325,632 tokens / 8.70 GiB (eager) vs 309,248 tokens / 8.26 GiB (graphs, 0.41 GiB graph memory): 5.0 percent less capacity; both equal tokens x 28,672 bytes.
step7_pilot.eager_first_trial_faster: In both eager-on runs the first trial was faster than later trials at 1K (0.28-0.30 s vs 0.31 s) and at 4K in the repeat; not seen with graphs. Cause unknown (clocks, CPU state, allocator?), not tested.

observed_not_conclusions.pool: eager off: 309,248 tokens (0.41 GiB CUDA graph memory); eager on (pasted startup): 325,632 tokens

step5_run_caveats.sampling_defaults: The server log shows vLLM applied the model's generation_config.json defaults (repetition_penalty 1.1, top_k 20, top_p 0.8; temperature 0.7 was overridden by the request's temperature 0). Run 20261116T210839Z-d6a00143 therefore ran with repetition_penalty 1.1 and is a pipeline-verification run, not a baseline. Fixed in code: the launcher now passes --generation-config vllm (the flag the server's own log message suggested; confirm it is accepted on the next launch).
step5_run_caveats.host_resources_seen_in_log: vLLM reported Available RAM 6.18 GiB and reduced Torch threads from 2 to 1. Host RAM bounds any CPU-offload experiment (Step 9), and a client load generator shares these few CPU cores with the server (Step 8).
benign_log_messages: FA2 unsupported on compute capability < 8 (an ERROR line, but vLLM falls back to TRITON_ATTN)
bfloat16 to float16 casting of checkpoint weights
FlashInfer top-p/top-k sampler unavailable on compute capability 7.5, falls back
'force killing remaining processes' and a leaked-semaphore warning at server shutdown
step5_run_caveats.metrics_endpoint: The server's route table lists /metrics, /health and /load, so engine cache usage and running/waiting counts should be readable in Step 6.
